operations_plan.summary: Edit the ring-end hole definition so that Sketch4 uses the existing circular-hole geometry as construction geometry for a concentric inscribed regular hexagon.

steps.description: Locate Sketch4 and confirm that it defines the cylindrical through-hole in the closed ring head. Associate the sketch with the ring-end bore represented by cylindrical face 21. Retrieve the bore center, thickness-direction axis, and original radius from the sketch or circular boundary; the identified bore has a 10 mm radius and is concentric with the outer ring profile. Sketch4 is not explicitly mapped in model.json, so face 21 and its circular boundary edges are the fallback references if the named sketch cannot be resolved directly.

Open Sketch4 on its existing ring-head support plane. If the support must be reconstructed, use the planar top face 24 at the ring head, with the sketch normal parallel to the original bore axis and part-thickness direction. Preserve the original hole center by projecting or externally referencing the center and circular boundary of the existing 10 mm-radius hole.

Convert the original 10 mm-radius circle to construction geometry, or recreate an equivalent construction circle from its referenced center and radius. Do not retain the circle as an active cut profile. This construction circle establishes the circumcircle for the replacement polygon.

Create a closed six-sided regular polygon centered coincident with the original bore center. Define it as inscribed in the original circle by constraining all six vertices to the 10 mm-radius construction circle. Apply equal-length constraints to the six sides and regular-polygon angular constraints. The resulting hexagon has a 10 mm circumradius, 20 mm across opposite vertices, approximately 17.3205 mm across opposite flats, and 10 mm side length.

Constrain the hexagon against rotation while preserving symmetry about the wrench longitudinal center plane. Because the request does not specify polygon rotation, use a symmetric default orientation with one pair of opposite vertices on the longitudinal centerline, unless Sketch4 contains an existing orientation reference that should be retained. Confirm that the sketch contains one active closed hexagonal region and that the original circle is construction-only.

operations_plan.summary: Replace the original cylindrical hole cut with a through-all cut driven by the new inscribed hexagonal Sketch4 profile.

steps.description: Edit the existing hole-generating cut feature so its selected profile is the active hexagonal region from the revised Sketch4. Remove the circular region from the cut selection. Perform this as a replacement of the original feature definition, or suppress/delete the original cylindrical cut before creating the new cut; do not apply a hexagonal cut to the already circularly cut result, because that would not restore the material between the inscribed hexagon and the former circle.

Set the subtractive extrusion end condition to Through All along the original hole axis, normal to Sketch4 and parallel to the part-thickness direction. Ensure the cut traverses the complete 15 mm wrench thickness from top face 24 to bottom face 25. If required by the CAD system, use a symmetric through-all or both-directions through-all condition so the cut remains valid regardless of sketch-plane placement.

Regenerate the part and verify that cylindrical bore face 21 is removed and replaced by six full-depth planar internal faces forming one regular hexagonal opening. Confirm that the hexagonal opening is concentric with the former hole, its six vertices lie on the original 10 mm-radius circle, and no residual circular cut surfaces remain.

Validate preservation of all non-target geometry. Keep the outer ring perimeter and neck transitions represented by faces 12, 11, and 13 unchanged; preserve the handle side rails 10 and 14, recessed panel faces 0 through 8, continuous top and bottom faces 24 and 25 outside the new opening, and the complete open-jaw head geometry represented by faces 9 and 15 through 23 except for obsolete bore face 21. Confirm that solid 0 remains one valid monolithic solid.
